ruled: COMMON IS THE INTERFACE LABEL OF THE THEME WHOSE ID IS `legacy`, BY ALIAS. Wherever a person reads a theme's name — a theme picker, a page's note, a report line — the theme with id `legacy` is labelled Common. The id stays `legacy` (and `apollo-legacy`) everywhere it is an identifier: tokens, canon.css selectors, file names, metas, rulings and packs. The one home of the display name is the `label` field of knowledge/tokens/themes/_themes.json, now 'Apollo Common' (was 'Apollo Legacy'); every interface reads it, and the picker prints it less 'Apollo '. Dave's words in chat #308 at 12:08 BST, verbatim: "Common is legacy - its how we should label it in any interfaces, we can rename or alias it, whatever is the best solutio". He left the mechanism to the build ('we can rename or alias it, whatever is the best solutio'); the #308 conductor chose ALIAS, NOT RENAME, because a rename would move hundreds of files and rewrite old records, and s227-D8 already keeps the full rename as its own lane. It also settles the question W-308i1 carried: 'Common' in s308-D2 means `legacy`, so the tree's chosen mark is red in Supercharge and Legacy/Common, black in Console and Mono. RECORD: enacted by #308 lane L — the registry label, the showroom and pack theme picker, the foundations pages, and a guard in gen_showroom.py --check that refuses a picker printing anything but the label. History (old review pages, rulings, reports) is untouched.
